dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function X, this is its totalized Bochner integral ∫ X dμ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the mean m = ∫ X dμ used to center X and also supplies the integrals occurring inside LocalDef002 and LocalDef004.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function Y, this is sqrt(∫ Y(ω)^2 dμ), using the totalized integral and Real.sqrt.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is applied to Y(ω) = X(ω) - ∫ X dμ, so the left side of the first equality is sqrt(∫ (X-m)^2 dμ).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For X, this is defined to be sqrt(LocalDef004 μ X).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the right side of the second equality definitionally the same expression as its left side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For X, this is the totalized integral ∫ (X(ω) - ∫ X dμ)^2 dμ, the centered second moment.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its square root is the right side of the first equality and both sides of the second equality after unfolding LocalDef003.

dependency_coverage.name: AddCommMonoidWithOne.toAddMonoidWithOne

dependency_coverage.name: And

dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of nonnegative extended real numbers, NNReal with an added top element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The MemLp exponent 2 and the value eLpNorm X 2 μ live in ENNReal, and finiteness is expressed by being strictly below top.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is propositional equality between two objects of the same type.

dependency_coverage.meaning: MemLp X 2 μ means that X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and eLpNorm X 2 μ < ∞.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the sole explicit premise about X. In the probability setting it gives the usual L² integrability context, although the stated equalities themselves are definitional and do not use this premise semantically.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instNeZeroSucc

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt

binders: Ω is an arbitrary type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
μ is a measure on Ω, equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
X is an arbitrary function Ω → ℝ.
hypotheses: μ is a probability measure, so μ(Ω)=1.
X belongs to MemLp at exponent 2 with respect to μ: X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and eLpNorm X 2 μ < ∞.
conclusions: Writing m = ∫Ω X dμ and v = ∫Ω (X(ω)-m)^2 dμ, the first conjunct is sqrt(∫Ω (X(ω)-m)^2 dμ) = sqrt(v), hence after unfolding the definitions it is the reflexive equality sqrt(v)=sqrt(v).
With the same v, the second conjunct is sqrt(v) = LocalDef003 μ X; since LocalDef003 μ X is defined as sqrt(v), this too is the reflexive equality sqrt(v)=sqrt(v).
mathematical_definitions: m := ∫Ω X(ω) dμ(ω), using Lean's totalized real-valued Bochner integral.
v := ∫Ω (X(ω)-m)^2 dμ(ω), again using the totalized Bochner integral.
LocalDef002 μ Y := sqrt(∫Ω Y(ω)^2 dμ(ω)); for Y=X-m this equals sqrt(v).
Real.sqrt(v) is sqrt(max(v,0)); in particular it is 0 for nonpositive input.
MemLp X 2 μ means AEStronglyMeasurable X μ together with eLpNorm X 2 μ < ⊤.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued L² function X on an arbitrary probability space, if m is its integral and v is the integral of (X-m)², then the square root of the integral of the squared centered function equals sqrt(v), and sqrt(v) equals the quantity defined to be sqrt(v). Both asserted equalities reduce by unfolding the supplied definitions to sqrt(v)=sqrt(v).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement applies only when the implicit probability-measure instance and the explicit MemLp X 2 μ premise are available; otherwise it asserts nothing for that choice of data.
No pointwise measurability hypothesis is stated. MemLp supplies almost-everywhere strong measurability instead.

The Bochner integral is totalized: outside integrable cases it denotes 0 rather than being undefined. Thus the formulas themselves remain meaningful even without integrability, although the L² probability-space hypothesis supplies the usual finite-mean and integrable-centered-square setting.

Real.sqrt is totalized by truncating negative inputs to 0. The statement does not separately assert that v is nonnegative, although in the stated L² setting v is the integral of an integrable nonnegative square and has the usual nonnegative interpretation.

Neither equality establishes a substantive analytic identity: the first repeats the expansion of LocalDef002 and LocalDef004, and the second repeats the definition of LocalDef003. The MemLp and probability hypotheses are not needed for these definitional equalities.
No assertion is made about positivity, nondegeneracy, variance being zero only for almost-everywhere constant functions, or any equality involving an L² norm as a separate library object.
